passage: Session note, Tuesday. Karthik arrived shaking with anger. Sabina, his partner in their small design studio, had moved the two biggest clients to her own new firm without telling him. He said he wanted to post everything about her online and "make sure nobody hires her again." I asked him to hold that thought for a day and not send anything tonight. We listed what he could do instead: gather the emails and contracts in one folder, read the partnership agreement, and book a consultation with a lawyer. He stopped pacing about halfway through. Before leaving he said, "I can be furious and still not do something I'll regret." I will check in on Friday to see whether the folder exists.

qa.q: What had Sabina done to make Karthik so angry?
qa.a: Sabina had moved the two biggest clients to her own new firm without telling him.

qa.q: What was Karthik feeling and wanting at the start of the session?
qa.a: He felt furious and wanted to expose Sabina online so nobody would hire her again.

qa.q: What calm steps did the narrator suggest to protect Karthik and his work?
qa.a: Gather the emails and contracts in one folder, read the partnership agreement and book a consultation with a lawyer.

qa.q: What would change for Karthik's own studio if he had posted the attacks that night?
qa.a: His time and attention would likely go into the fight instead of the work and the clients he still has, and it could weaken his position.

grounding: Shows a business owner raging at a partner's betrayal and considering revenge, guided towards calm, documented steps.
